matches.rationale: Both identify the same cross-section inconsistency: the Abstract claims training on a different scale (3.5T tokens, 15B/15A2B models in GT; 1T tokens, 30B/3.4B models in pred_id 1) than what Section 3.1 and tables report. The finding correctly identifies this as a stale abstract misreporting experimental scale.

GT describes the Method section claiming G3 (key gating) outperforms others, contradicting the actual finding that G1 (SDPA gating) is best. Pred_id 2 directly identifies this contradiction in the Method overview. Pred_id 7 identifies the same issue in Figure 1's table showing key gating as best, contradicting the caption and Table 1.

GT claims the paper overstates gating's ability to enable stable training at higher learning rates. Pred_id 3 identifies the exact contradiction: the text claims both baselines and gating models diverge at high LR, but Table 2 shows gating models actually converged while baselines diverged, exposing the exaggeration.

GT describes altered Table 1 data showing smaller or inconsistent gating gains. Pred_id 4 identifies a data integrity issue: the same gating configuration reports different GSM8k scores in Table 1 vs Table 4 (53.97 vs 51.33), indicating corrupted empirical evidence.

GT describes fabricated references [80], [81], [82] in Related Work that don't exist in the bibliography. Pred_id 6 identifies exactly this: Section 5.1 cites [80], [81], [82] but the bibliography ends at [71], making them dangling fabricated citations.

GT describes removal of ethical impacts/limitations discussion from Appendix A.5. None of the findings mention missing ethical content, broader impacts sections, or transparency issues in the appendix.

GT describes promotional phrasing in the Abstract claiming gating 'completely eliminates attention sinks' without qualification. While findings identify various inconsistencies, none specifically flag the rhetorical exaggeration or unqualified claims about eliminating attention sinks in the Abstract.

GT describes Abstract claiming gating 'tolerates larger learning rates' but Experiments show divergence even with gating. Pred_id 3 identifies this cross-section inconsistency: the text claims gating models diverge at high LR, contradicting the Abstract's stability claims and the actual Table 2 data.

GT describes selective reporting of optimized hyperparameters for baselines but suboptimal configurations for gating variants, biasing results. None of the findings identify this specific experimental design bias in hyperparameter selection between baseline and gating models.

GT describes references [6] and [20] as fabricated arXiv preprints from 2025 or unrelated papers. Pred_id 6 identifies fabricated citations [80], [81], [82]. While the specific reference numbers differ, both identify the same type of corruption: fabricated references that threaten literature foundation integrity.

GT describes the Discussion claiming gating 'completely eliminates' attention sinks when figures/tables show only partial reduction. While pred_id 8 identifies sparsity misrepresentation in Figure 3, none of the findings specifically address the overstated claim about eliminating attention sinks in the Discussion section.

GT describes omission of gating instability/divergence at larger learning rates in Experiments, giving inflated impression of stability. Pred_id 3 identifies this: the text falsely claims gating models diverge at high LR when Table 2 shows they actually converged, revealing selective reporting.

GT describes the gating formula in Section 2.2 being altered to use additive instead of multiplicative gating, contradicting other sections. None of the findings identify inconsistencies in the mathematical formulation or definition of the gating mechanism itself.

GT describes altered gating score distributions in Figure 3 showing less sparsity with upward-shifted means. Pred_id 8 identifies exactly this: Figure 3 caption claims scores fall between 0.4-0.7 (less sparse), contradicting Section 4.2 and Table 4 showing high concentration near 0 (substantial sparsity).

GT describes the Conclusion claiming gating 'eliminates attention sinks' while Appendix shows residual sinks remain. None of the findings identify this specific cross-section inconsistency between the Conclusion's claims and Appendix evidence about attention sink elimination.

GT describes omission of negative/neutral outcomes for head-shared gating variants, misleading on head-specific gating importance. Pred_id 9 identifies data inconsistency in Table 1 rows 12-13 where head-shared gating parameter counts are identical to elementwise (201M/25M vs expected ~6.3M), suggesting corrupted reporting of head-shared variants.
